description: The radar chart that labels its rings, tells you what its axis is doing, and lets every spoke have its own scale. Radar and spider charts are easy to draw and easy to misread. A missing value drawn at the centre reads as zero. One large measure squashes every other spoke into the middle. A slicer re-sorts the axes under the reader. Radar & Polar Pro deals with each of these, adds targets, and says on the chart what it did. THREE SCALES, EACH FOR A REASON • One scale for all spokes, the default, because that is how a radar is read. When one spoke dwarfs the rest, a note names it and the setting to change. • Each spoke its own range, for mixed units: revenue, NPS and a 1 to 5 rating on one web. • Percent of each spoke's target: the target is one circle, the rings read in percent of target, and an overshoot moves the rim out on every spoke, so nothing is flattened against it. • A fixed business range for any spoke, such as −100 to 100 for NPS, and a logarithmic axis with rings on round values. TARGETS AND THE GAP Bind a Target field and choose an outline, a shaded band or markers. Switch on the gap and the distance to target is drawn on every spoke, green where met, red where missed, with the signed difference as a label.
